videos.script: Microservices were not the first attempt at building a system out of services, and they will not be the last. {{history}} This lesson looks at three neighbours. Service-oriented architecture, which came first and put the intelligence in the middle. {{soa}} Serverless functions, where the platform runs your code only while an event needs it, and charges you for exactly that. {{serverless}} And the service mesh, which takes the network chores out of every service and gives them to a proxy standing beside it. {{mesh}} Each one moves work from your code to somebody else's machinery. {{moves}} You will time a cold start on your own machine, and see why a function that was idle makes its first caller wait. {{cold}} You will do the arithmetic of paying per request, and find the volume where an always-on machine becomes cheaper. {{cost}} And you will finish with a table of which shape fits which force. None of the three is a step up from the others. They are answers to different questions.
